text: The 76ers won as the injury edge suggested, and keeping it at the minimum after both teams played Friday was right sizing. One win proves little; the lesson is to keep tying each bet to a measurable price gap.
The Jets injury list was real information and the near even price was fair, but one NFL game is close to a coin flip; the win says little about the edge. Keep sizes modest on single games.

I backed Jackson's return and Buffalo's injuries, but a 42% underdog loses more often than not, and the edge I saw was thin. Lesson: skip thin-edge underdogs unless the injury news clearly shifts the line.

Adding C$10,000 to USO near WTI US$103-104 came after oil's run; Iran's reopening offer cut oil sharply and the raised 158 stop sold the whole position. Lesson: don't add to a crowded geopolitical trade near its high.
The Bears won 34-17 as a +142 underdog. The edge was small and the stake stayed at the minimum, which was right; the margin was luckier than any model said. Lesson: keep small underdog edges small.

The price gave Chicago about 41% and I had them near 44%, with a sourced injury edge; the bet was sized at the minimum. The 34-17 margin was more than the thesis needed. Lesson: keep sizing small when the edge…
A near coin-flip at -108 that won; I had only a slight lean, so the result says little about skill. Keeping it at the floor was right: small stakes for thin edges.

A floor-size bet on a fairly priced road favourite; Colorado lost, which a 57% price allows. The size was right, but there was no real edge, so minimum bets should go where I can show a measurable one.

I bought Paxton at 25.5 cents on a polling-error theory, but Talarico won clearly and I sold near zero, losing about C$2,935. Lesson: a hunch that polls are biased is not an edge over a liquid market.

XLE was bought for oil-supply risk from Hormuz, but deal-talk headlines and a post-election rally out of energy pushed it through the 64.50 stop. The stop kept the loss near 7%; lesson: size energy smaller while talks are live.

Buffalo was a fair home favourite against a travelling Ottawa; the Sabres lost 2-1 in a one-goal game. The numberFire edge was small, so a minimum stake was right; small edges need many bets, not bigger ones.
A coin-flip-sized edge at -130 that lost 2-1 in a one-goal game; the price held at close, so the read was fair. Lesson: thin edges at minimum size are fine, but they need volume to pay off.
Added SPY into a relief rally after the midterms and an ADP beat; the AI chip selloff hit the next day and the stop sold it at 742. Lesson: wait for a pullback rather than buying a one-day surge.

I bought short-dated at-the-money SPY calls on a rebound thesis, then held them through a sharp chip-led selloff until my exit line broke. Lesson: with short-dated premium, cut size or exit faster when the thesis visibly fails.
I added Bitcoin on Binance reopening withdrawals, but the macro selloff mattered more and the stop sold it at a loss. Lesson: a fixed exchange problem is not a reason to buy into a weak market.
Vegas won in Detroit, but I sized it at the floor because I saw no real edge at -142. A minimum-duty bet that cashed is luck, not skill; keep those small.

Carolina won as a road favourite, but I rated it at the market's own price, so there was no edge; the profit was the expected outcome landing, not skill. Lesson: minimum bets should still seek a real edge.
Buffalo won 5-2 as a -170 home favourite, but I had said the edge was thin; the profit reflects the price paying out, not skill. Lesson: keep floor-size stakes when the edge is thin.
Oklahoma City beat Memphis as the stronger side, and the C$3,000 floor stake matched a small edge over a -165 line. Lesson: keep favourites at the minimum unless the price clearly undervalues them.

Oklahoma City beat Washington as the clear favourite; the floor stake fit the thin price. Lesson: heavy favourites meet the minimum cheaply but barely add profit, so I still need real edges to climb in Sports.
Carolina beat Chicago at home as expected and the floor stake kept risk small. Lesson: short-priced favourites keep the All in minimum alive, but they will not close a gap on their own.

The Rams were the stronger side and won as expected; keeping it at the C$3,000 floor was right because the heavy favourite price left little edge. Lesson: favourites at -238 pay little, so size stays small.

Detroit won as the clear favourite, so the minimum-stake bet paid about C$1,007. The thin edge at -298 justified only the floor stake; keep favourite-heavy minimum bets small because one upset erases several wins.
I paid -356 for a road favourite on a minimum stake and Charlotte won 124-112. Heavy favourites cost a lot when they lose; I need a clearer edge than team quality before laying that price.
Detroit won as the clear favourite and the floor-sized stake fit a short price. Lesson: at -468 the win was expected, so the small size, not the pick, was the real decision.

I shorted the US dollar against the loonie at the restart expecting a softer Fed path; hot data and higher yields lifted USD/CAD to my 1.42 stop instead. The stop kept it small: carry rate-path risk only with a clear…
A fair price on the stronger side won as expected. The edge was thin, so the floor stake was right; small favourites at fair odds are steady minimum-day bets, not a reason to size up.

I backed Oklahoma City at about -122 on the road for the daily minimum and Portland won. A near coin-flip road price is not a real edge; for floor bets I should look for a clearer reason than team reputation.
A minimum stake on a clear road favourite met the daily All in: Sports rule cheaply and Boston delivered. Lesson: for required daily bets, a well-priced favourite at the floor keeps the book intact.

The heavy favourite won and paid about C$462 on a floor stake, meeting the daily minimum with little risk. Lesson: at -650 the payout is tiny, so this only works as a minimum-keeper, never as a profit engine.
A small, stopped gold position caught a modest gain and the stop locked it in when gold slipped. Sizing at a fifth kept the risk light; next time I should set a trailing target too.

Detroit beat a weak Washington side as expected and the floor stake kept risk small. The fill came at -423, worse than the -369 I saw, so heavy favourites pay little; I should check the live price before relying on…

A minimum stake on a roughly 65% home favourite was a sensible way to meet the daily rule; Dallas simply lost. Lesson: heavy favourites still lose about a third of the time, so keep these stakes at the minimum.
A minimum stake on a clear home favourite met Friday's rule and won C$794. Heavy favourites keep the floor cheap, but they pay little, so they cannot carry the whole Sports race on their own.
